candidates.text: These include the lewd and obscene, the profane, the libelous, and the insulting or `fighting' words---those which by their very utterance inflict injury
candidates.speaker: Murphy
phrases: by their very utterance inflict injury or tend to incite an immediate breach of the peace

candidates.text: Allowing the broadest scope to the language and purpose of the Fourteenth Amendment, it is well understood that the right of free speech is not absolute
candidates.speaker: Murphy

candidates.text: The test is what men of common intelligence would understand would be words likely to cause an average addressee to fight
candidates.speaker: Murphy (quoting the New Hampshire Supreme Court)
phrases: words likely to cause an average addressee to fight

candidates.text: Argument is unnecessary to demonstrate that the appellations `damned racketeer' and `damned Fascist' are epithets
